$comment: Swift<->JS public-surface parity map. Keys under `symbols` are CadenceCore selectors as check-parity.mjs extracts them (funcs and inits keyed with external labels; stored fields and enum cases are out of scope in v1, and an init that only assigns stored fields is listed `swiftOnly` for the same reason). A value is the JS export twin (string), {"js": export, "note": why-the-shape-differs}, or {"swiftOnly": reason}. `webOnly` lists JS exports with no twin in the module's Swift file; the reason names the Swift counterpart elsewhere, if there is one. Every export of `js` must be accounted for; modules that share a `js` file each list the `// ---- Section ----` headers they own in `jsSections` and account for the exports under those.

PlateThemeID.note: enum cases as a frozen id array

PlateThemeID.id.swiftOnly: Identifiable conformance; JS ids are the strings themselves

PlateFinish.swiftOnly: typed enum; JS carries finish as a string inside plateThemeMaterial()

PlateHubFinish.swiftOnly: typed enum; JS carries hub finish as a string in PLATE_THEMES

BarFinish.swiftOnly: typed enum; JS carries bar finish as a string in PLATE_THEMES

PlateMaterial.swiftOnly: value type; JS returns a plain object from plateThemeMaterial()

PlateMaterial.init(finish:metal:roughnes.swiftOnly: memberwise init; JS builds the plain object directly

PlateRatios.swiftOnly: value type; JS returns a plain object from plateThemeRatios()

PlateTheme.note: struct + static `all` table vs frozen theme table

webOnly.plateThemeInventory: inventory merge; the Swift twin is Gym.applyPlateProfileInventory() in the app target, outside CadenceCore
